VBO:0201397.summary: Water Spaniels bring different characters to a water-working heritage. The Irish Water Spaniel is loyal, alert and playful, with a sense of humour and some reserve toward strangers. The American Water Spaniel is friendly and eager to please, yet energetic in the hunt. Both retrieve game from water; the American was developed to work from small boats as well as on land.
VBO:0201397.shortDescription: Water-working spaniels include the playful, loyal Irish breed and the eager American hunter, each with its own character.

sources.title: American Spaniel Club — Cocker Spaniel club flyer
sources.evidence: Actual entire two-page ASC2006 flyer read. History explicitly divides early spaniels into land and water groups; subsequent cockers/toys history concerns land spaniels. Used only to establish historical broader branch, not to transfer Cocker merry/affectionate temperament to Water Spaniels.

sources.title: American Kennel Club — English Cocker Spaniel vs Cocker Spaniel
sources.evidence: Actual complete How the Two Breeds Developed section read, including actual traditional land/water spaniel division according to where they worked, and attributed breed-club presidents on land-size branches. Other Cocker temperament/anatomy not used for Water Spaniels.

sources.title: FCI Standard124 — Irish Water Spaniel
sources.evidence: Actual entire five-page English standard read. Named Irish breed intelligent/enduring/eager/loyal with humour and discernment toward strangers; waterfowling and cover retrieval. Full head/eyes/ears/topknot, barrel body, broad level back, powerful legs/feet, crisp rich puce-liver curls and intact rat-tail naturally shorter than hock and nearly level read. Speculative Persia/Spain/indigenous ancestry omitted.

sources.title: FCI Standard301 — American Water Spaniel
sources.evidence: Actual entire five-page English standard read. Named American breed friendly, intelligent, eager to please, energetic but controllable in hunt; developed to retrieve from skiff/canoes and work ground. Own wavy/curly coat, smaller body and moderate feathered rocker tail read but not mixed into IWS representative.

sources.title: Irish Water Spaniel Club of America — illustrated breed standard
sources.evidence: Actual printed4–14,18,20–25,28–30 substantive history, appearance, adult body/head/size, legs/feet, rat-tail, coat and temperament paragraphs read. Explicit historic land/water varieties and Irish breed development; no precise ancient origins/uncertain cross ancestry copied. Actual printed28–29 alert/inquisitive/active humour, loyal devotion and familiar exuberance versus stranger reserve read. Printed21 tail smooth part natural, not clipping; whole PDF retained, not every illustration or page claimed inspected.
